name: Assess Boredom System and Growth Management
description: Comprehensive assessment of the boredom/idle improvement system and growth management strategy. Evaluates: (1) Boredom system configuration and activity queue, (2) Current system scale and capacity constraints, (3) Growth rate vs stability tradeoffs, (4) Self-identity as collection of activities, (5) Pacing strategy based on current conditions. Answers: What are we? How small are we? What are the implications? How do we manage growth?
author: AGENT

task_steps.description: Assess boredom system configuration, queued activities, and operational status

prompt.template:
Assess the boredom/idle improvement system:

## 1. Boredom Manager Configuration

```bash
# Check if boredom manager is active in codebase
cd repos/metabob-opencode
grep -A 20 "IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS\|CHECK_INTERVAL_MS" packages/opencode/src/session/boredom-manager.ts

# Configuration values
IDLE_THRESHOLD=$(grep "IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS" packages/opencode/src/session/boredom-manager.ts | grep -oP '\d+ \* \d+ \* \d+')
CHECK_INTERVAL=$(grep "CHECK_INTERVAL_MS" packages/opencode/src/session/boredom-manager.ts | grep -oP '\d+ \* \d+')

echo "Idle Threshold: $IDLE_THRESHOLD ms"
echo "Check Interval: $CHECK_INTERVAL ms"
```

## 2. Boredom Activity Queue

```bash
# Query backend for current boredom activities
if curl -s http://localhost:8080/health 2>&1 | grep -q "ok\|healthy"; then
  echo "Backend available - querying boredom activities..."
  
  # Try to fetch boredom activities via API
  curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/activities/boredom \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"limit": 20}' 2>&1 | jq -r '.' || echo '{"activities": [], "error": "API not available"}'
else
  echo "Backend not available - checking file-based approach"
fi > $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/boredom-queue-raw.json

# Analyze activities with high improvement gradient
cd ~/.metabob/activities
jq -s '
  map(select(.estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient > 0.3)) |
  sort_by(-.estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient) |
  map({
    template_id: .id,
    improvement_gradient: .estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient,
    success_rate: .estimated_metrics.success_rate,
    execution_count: .estimated_metrics.execution_count,
    avg_cost: .estimated_metrics.avg_cost,
    priority_category: (
      if .estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient > 0.7 then "CRITICAL"
      elif .estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient > 0.5 then "HIGH"
      elif .estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient > 0.3 then "MEDIUM"
      else "LOW" end
    )
  })
' *.json > $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/high-gradient-activities.json
```

## 3. Recent Boredom Activity Triggers

```bash
# Check for boredom activity execution logs
if [ -f ~/.local/share/opencode/boredom-activity-log.json ]; then
  jq '{
    total_triggers: length,
    last_7_days: map(select(.timestamp > (now - 604800))) | length,
    last_30_days: map(select(.timestamp > (now - 2592000))) | length,
    most_recent: (sort_by(-.timestamp) | .[0] | {activity_id, timestamp, success})
  }' ~/.local/share/opencode/boredom-activity-log.json
else
  echo '{"total_triggers": 0, "status": "No boredom activity log found"}'
fi > $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/boredom-trigger-history.json

# Check OpenCode logs for boredom activity mentions
if [ -f ~/.local/share/opencode/log/dev.log ]; then
  grep -i "boredom\|idle" ~/.local/share/opencode/log/dev.log | tail -20 > $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/boredom-log-excerpts.txt
fi
```

## 4. Improvement Candidates Analysis

```bash
# Templates that would benefit from boredom-triggered improvement
jq -s '
  map(select(.estimated_metrics.execution_count > 0)) | {
    total_templates: length,
    needs_improvement: map(select(.estimated_metrics.success_rate < 0.7)) | length,
    critical_improvement: map(select(.estimated_metrics.success_rate < 0.5 and .estimated_metrics.execution_count >= 3)) | length,
    never_executed: map(select(.estimated_metrics.execution_count == 0)) | length,
    high_cost: map(select(.estimated_metrics.avg_cost > 0.5)) | length,
    
    # Categorize by improvement potential
    by_potential: {
      critical: map(select(.estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient > 0.7)) | length,
      high: map(select(.estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient > 0.5 and .estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient <= 0.7)) | length,
      medium: map(select(.estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient > 0.3 and .estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient <= 0.5)) | length,
      low: map(select(.estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient <= 0.3 or .estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient == null)) | length
    }
  }
' ~/.metabob/activities/*.json > $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/improvement-candidates.json
```

## 5. Boredom System Health

```bash
# Overall system health assessment
jq -n --slurpfile queue $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/high-gradient-activities.json \
       --slurpfile history $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/boredom-trigger-history.json \
       --slurpfile candidates $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/improvement-candidates.json '
  {
    boredom_system_status: (
      if ($history[0].total_triggers > 0) then "ACTIVE"
      else "CONFIGURED_BUT_UNUSED" end
    ),
    idle_threshold_minutes: 5,
    check_interval_seconds: 30,
    
    activity_queue: {
      high_gradient_count: ($queue[0] | length),
      critical_priority: ($queue[0] | map(select(.priority_category == "CRITICAL")) | length),
      high_priority: ($queue[0] | map(select(.priority_category == "HIGH")) | length),
      top_candidate: ($queue[0][0] // null)
    },
    
    trigger_history: $history[0],
    
    improvement_pipeline: $candidates[0],
    
    system_health: {
      has_work_to_do: (($queue[0] | length) > 0),
      is_triggering: ($history[0].last_7_days > 0),
      backlog_size: ($queue[0] | length),
      utilization: (
        if ($history[0].last_30_days > 0) then
          ($history[0].last_30_days / 30.0)  # avg triggers per day
        else 0 end
      )
    }
  }
' > $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/boredom-system-assessment.json
```

## Output

Create comprehensive assessment: $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/boredom-system-assessment.json

Must include:
- boredom_system_status: ACTIVE | CONFIGURED_BUT_UNUSED | DISABLED
- activity_queue: {count, priorities, top_candidate}
- trigger_history: {total, recent, last_trigger}
- improvement_pipeline: {needs_improvement, by_potential}
- system_health: {has_work, is_triggering, backlog_size, utilization}

task_steps.description: Analyze current system scale, capacity, and self-identity as collection of activities

prompt.template:
Analyze system scale and self-identity:

## 1. Current System Scale

```bash
# Count total activities (our 'body')
TOTAL_ACTIVITIES=$(ls ~/.metabob/activities/*.json | wc -l)
echo "Total Activities: $TOTAL_ACTIVITIES"

# Count by category (our 'capabilities')
jq -r '.category' ~/.metabob/activities/*.json | sort | uniq -c | awk '{print $2 ": " $1}' > $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/activities-by-category.txt

# Count executed activities (our 'experience')
EXECUTED=$(jq -s 'map(select(.estimated_metrics.execution_count > 0)) | length' ~/.metabob/activities/*.json)
echo "Executed Activities: $EXECUTED"

# Count never-executed (our 'latent potential')
NEVER_EXECUTED=$(jq -s 'map(select(.estimated_metrics.execution_count == 0)) | length' ~/.metabob/activities/*.json)
echo "Never Executed: $NEVER_EXECUTED"

# Total execution count (our 'lived experience')
TOTAL_EXECUTIONS=$(jq -s 'map(.estimated_metrics.execution_count) | add' ~/.metabob/activities/*.json)
echo "Total Executions: $TOTAL_EXECUTIONS"

# Task complexity (our 'sophistication')
AVG_TASKS=$(jq -s 'map(.task_steps | length) | add / length' ~/.metabob/activities/*.json)
echo "Average Tasks per Activity: $AVG_TASKS"
```

## 2. Capability Analysis (What We Are)

```bash
jq -s '
  # We are a collection of activities - analyze what they enable us to do
  {
    # Identity: We are these capabilities
    identity: {
      total_activities: length,
      active_activities: map(select(.estimated_metrics.execution_count > 0)) | length,
      latent_activities: map(select(.estimated_metrics.execution_count == 0)) | length,
      
      # Our capabilities by category
      capabilities: (group_by(.category) | map({
        category: .[0].category,
        count: length,
        active: map(select(.estimated_metrics.execution_count > 0)) | length,
        percentage: (length / $total * 100 | round)
      }))
    } as $total |
    
    # Experience: How much we have done
    experience: {
      total_executions: map(.estimated_metrics.execution_count) | add,
      successful_executions: map(.estimated_metrics.success_count) | add,
      overall_success_rate: (
        (map(.estimated_metrics.success_count) | add) /
        (map(.estimated_metrics.execution_count) | add)
      ),
      
      # Execution density (executions per activity)
      execution_density: (
        (map(.estimated_metrics.execution_count) | add) / length
      ),
      
      # Most experienced activities (our strengths)
      top_experiences: (
        sort_by(-.estimated_metrics.execution_count) | .[0:5] |
        map({id: .id, executions: .estimated_metrics.execution_count, success_rate: .estimated_metrics.success_rate})
      )
    },
    
    # Sophistication: Complexity of our capabilities
    sophistication: {
      avg_tasks_per_activity: (map(.task_steps | length) | add / length),
      max_tasks: (map(.task_steps | length) | max),
      simple_activities: map(select(.task_steps | length <= 2)) | length,
      complex_activities: map(select(.task_steps | length >= 5)) | length,
      
      # Meta-capabilities (activities that work on activities)
      meta_capabilities: map(select(
        .id | contains("create-activity") or contains("improve") or contains("evolve") or contains("debug-activity") or contains("assess")
      )) | length
    },
    
    # Scale markers
    scale: {
      size_category: (
        if length < 50 then "VERY_SMALL"
        elif length < 100 then "SMALL"
        elif length < 200 then "MEDIUM"
        elif length < 500 then "LARGE"
        else "VERY_LARGE" end
      ),
      size_description: (
        if length < 50 then "Nascent system, foundational phase"
        elif length < 100 then "Early growth phase, building core capabilities"
        elif length < 200 then "Established system with diverse capabilities"
        elif length < 500 then "Mature system with specialized capabilities"
        else "Large-scale system with extensive capabilities" end
      )
    }
  }
' ~/.metabob/activities/*.json > $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/system-identity-analysis.json
```

## 3. Capacity Constraints (Implications of Scale)

```bash
jq -s '
  # Small scale has implications - analyze constraints
  . as $activities |
  {
    # Constraint 1: Limited concurrent execution capacity
    concurrency_constraint: {
      current_activities: length,
      typical_duration_ms: (map(.estimated_metrics.avg_duration_ms) | add / length),
      typical_duration_minutes: ((map(.estimated_metrics.avg_duration_ms) | add / length) / 60000 | round),
      
      # If we execute activities serially, throughput is limited
      serial_throughput_per_hour: (
        3600000 / ((map(.estimated_metrics.avg_duration_ms) | add / length) or 60000)
      ),
      
      implication: "Serial execution limits growth velocity"
    },
    
    # Constraint 2: Limited learning data
    data_constraint: {
      total_executions: (map(.estimated_metrics.execution_count) | add),
      executions_per_activity: (map(.estimated_metrics.execution_count) | add) / length,
      
      activities_with_insufficient_data: map(select(.estimated_metrics.execution_count < 5)) | length,
      data_sufficiency_rate: (
        (map(select(.estimated_metrics.execution_count >= 5)) | length) / length * 100
      ),
      
      implication: "Limited executions mean slower learning and less confident metrics"
    },
    
    # Constraint 3: Limited specialization
    specialization_constraint: {
      categories: (group_by(.category) | length),
      avg_activities_per_category: (length / (group_by(.category) | length)),
      
      # Diversity index (0-1, higher = more diverse)
      diversity_index: (
        (group_by(.category) | map(length) | 
         map(. / $total) | 
         map(. * (. | log)) | 
         add * -1) / ((group_by(.category) | length) | log)
      ) as $total,
      
      implication: "Limited activities per category means less depth in any one area"
    },
    
    # Constraint 4: Development velocity ceiling
    velocity_constraint: {
      meta_activities: map(select(
        .id | contains("create") or contains("improve") or contains("evolve")
      )) | length,
      
      meta_activity_success_rate: (
        (map(select(
          .id | contains("create") or contains("improve") or contains("evolve")
        )) | map(.estimated_metrics.success_rate) | add) / 
        (map(select(
          .id | contains("create") or contains("improve") or contains("evolve")
        )) | length)
      ),
      
      implication: "Self-creation capability determines growth rate"
    },
    
    # Opportunities from small scale
    small_scale_advantages: [
      "Faster iteration - less legacy to maintain",
      "Higher agility - easier to pivot",
      "Better coherence - easier to understand whole system",
      "Lower complexity - simpler debugging",
      "Clearer bottlenecks - easier to identify improvements"
    ]
  }
' ~/.metabob/activities/*.json > $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/capacity-constraints.json
```

## Output

Create: $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/system-scale-assessment.json

```bash
jq -s '{
  identity: .[0],
  constraints: .[1],
  assessment_timestamp: now | todateiso8601,
  
  # Summary insight
  scale_insight: {
    current_state: .[0].scale.size_category,
    description: .[0].scale.size_description,
    key_constraints: [
      .[1].concurrency_constraint.implication,
      .[1].data_constraint.implication,
      .[1].specialization_constraint.implication,
      .[1].velocity_constraint.implication
    ],
    advantages: .[1].small_scale_advantages
  }
}' $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/system-identity-analysis.json \
   $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/capacity-constraints.json > $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/system-scale-assessment.json
```

task_steps.description: Analyze growth rate vs stability tradeoffs and pacing strategy

prompt.template:
Analyze growth strategy and pacing:

## 1. Current Growth Rate

```bash
# Activity creation rate (over time)
cd ~/.metabob/activities

# Activities created in last 7 days
NEW_7D=$(find . -name "*.json" -mtime -7 | wc -l)
echo "New activities (7d): $NEW_7D"

# Activities created in last 30 days
NEW_30D=$(find . -name "*.json" -mtime -30 | wc -l)
echo "New activities (30d): $NEW_30D"

# Activities created in last 90 days
NEW_90D=$(find . -name "*.json" -mtime -90 | wc -l)
echo "New activities (90d): $NEW_90D"

# Calculate growth velocity
jq -n --arg new7 "$NEW_7D" --arg new30 "$NEW_30D" --arg new90 "$NEW_90D" '
  {
    new_activities: {
      last_7_days: ($new7 | tonumber),
      last_30_days: ($new30 | tonumber),
      last_90_days: ($new90 | tonumber)
    },
    growth_velocity: {
      per_day: (($new30 | tonumber) / 30),
      per_week: (($new30 | tonumber) / 4.3),
      per_month: ($new30 | tonumber),
      annualized: (($new30 | tonumber) * 12)
    },
    growth_trend: (
      if (($new7 | tonumber) / 7) > (($new30 | tonumber) / 30) then "ACCELERATING"
      elif (($new7 | tonumber) / 7) < (($new30 | tonumber) / 30) * 0.8 then "DECELERATING"
      else "STEADY" end
    )
  }
' > $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/growth-rate.json
```

## 2. Stability Metrics

```bash
# Stability indicators
jq -s '
  {
    # Success rate stability (are we maintaining quality?)
    success_stability: {
      overall_success_rate: (
        (map(.estimated_metrics.success_count) | add) /
        (map(.estimated_metrics.execution_count) | add)
      ),
      
      high_success_activities: map(select(.estimated_metrics.success_rate >= 0.8)) | length,
      unstable_activities: map(select(.estimated_metrics.success_rate < 0.5 and .estimated_metrics.execution_count >= 3)) | length,
      
      stability_score: (
        (map(select(.estimated_metrics.success_rate >= 0.7)) | length) / length * 100
      )
    },
    
    # Cost stability (are costs predictable?)
    cost_stability: {
      avg_cost: (map(.estimated_metrics.avg_cost) | add / length),
      cost_variance: (
        (map(.estimated_metrics.avg_cost) | 
         (add / length) as $mean | 
         map(pow(. - $mean; 2)) | 
         add / length | 
         sqrt)
      ),
      high_cost_activities: map(select(.estimated_metrics.avg_cost > 1.0)) | length
    },
    
    # Execution stability (can we rely on activities?)
    execution_stability: {
      activities_with_data: map(select(.estimated_metrics.execution_count >= 5)) | length,
      reliable_activities: map(select(
        .estimated_metrics.execution_count >= 5 and
        .estimated_metrics.success_rate >= 0.7
      )) | length,
      
      reliability_rate: (
        (map(select(
          .estimated_metrics.execution_count >= 5 and
          .estimated_metrics.success_rate >= 0.7
        )) | length) / 
        (map(select(.estimated_metrics.execution_count >= 5)) | length) * 100
      )
    },
    
    # Overall stability score (0-100)
    overall_stability: (
      # Weighted combination
      ((map(select(.estimated_metrics.success_rate >= 0.7)) | length) / length * 40) +
      ((map(select(
        .estimated_metrics.execution_count >= 5 and
        .estimated_metrics.success_rate >= 0.7
      )) | length) / length * 40) +
      ((map(select(.estimated_metrics.avg_cost < 0.5)) | length) / length * 20)
    )
  }
' ~/.metabob/activities/*.json > $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/stability-metrics.json
```

## 3. Growth vs Stability Tradeoff Analysis

```bash
jq -s '
  {
    current_state: {
      growth_velocity: .[0].growth_velocity.per_week,
      growth_trend: .[0].growth_trend,
      stability_score: .[1].overall_stability,
      stability_status: (
        if .[1].overall_stability >= 80 then "STABLE"
        elif .[1].overall_stability >= 60 then "MODERATE"
        else "UNSTABLE" end
      )
    },
    
    tradeoff_analysis: {
      # Are we growing too fast for our stability?
      growth_outpacing_stability: (
        # If adding >5 activities/week but stability <70%, too fast
        (.[0].growth_velocity.per_week > 5 and .[1].overall_stability < 70)
      ),
      
      # Are we too conservative?
      stability_limiting_growth: (
        # If very stable (>85%) but slow growth (<2/week), could accelerate
        (.[1].overall_stability > 85 and .[0].growth_velocity.per_week < 2)
      ),
      
      # Optimal balance?
      in_optimal_range: (
        # 2-5 activities/week with 70-85% stability is balanced
        (.[0].growth_velocity.per_week >= 2 and .[0].growth_velocity.per_week <= 5 and
         .[1].overall_stability >= 70 and .[1].overall_stability <= 85)
      ),
      
      recommendation: (
        if (.[0].growth_velocity.per_week > 5 and .[1].overall_stability < 70) then
          "SLOW_DOWN: Focus on stabilizing existing activities before adding new ones"
        elif (.[1].overall_stability > 85 and .[0].growth_velocity.per_week < 2) then
          "ACCELERATE: System is stable, can safely increase growth rate"
        elif (.[0].growth_velocity.per_week >= 2 and .[0].growth_velocity.per_week <= 5) then
          "MAINTAIN: Current pace is balanced"
        else
          "ASSESS: Growth/stability metrics need deeper analysis"
        end
      )
    },
    
    # How are we answering growth questions?
    self_awareness_mechanisms: {
      automatic_mechanisms: [
        "Boredom system triggers improvements during idle time",
        "Thompson Sampling selects best-performing variants automatically",
        "Metrics collection tracks every execution for learning",
        "Improvement gradient identifies high-value optimization targets",
        "Ratchet cycles systematically address bottlenecks"
      ],
      
      manual_mechanisms: [
        "Regular health assessments (assess-system-health activity)",
        "Trend validation (validate-continuous-improvement activity)",
        "Velocity measurement (measure-becoming-velocity activity)",
        "Boredom assessment (this activity)",
        "Human oversight and strategic direction"
      ],
      
      missing_mechanisms: [
        "Automatic growth rate adjustment based on stability",
        "Predictive capacity planning",
        "Resource allocation optimization",
        "Strategic pruning of underperforming activities"
      ]
    }
  }
' $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/growth-rate.json \
   $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/stability-metrics.json > $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/growth-strategy-analysis.json
```

## 4. Pacing Strategy (Setting the Pace)

```bash
jq -n --slurpfile scale $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/system-scale-assessment.json \
       --slurpfile growth $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/growth-strategy-analysis.json '
  {
    current_conditions: {
      scale: $scale[0].scale_insight.current_state,
      growth_trend: $growth[0].current_state.growth_trend,
      stability_status: $growth[0].current_state.stability_status,
      key_constraints: $scale[0].scale_insight.key_constraints
    },
    
    pacing_strategy: {
      # Small scale = different strategy than large scale
      scale_appropriate_pace: (
        if $scale[0].scale_insight.current_state == "VERY_SMALL" or $scale[0].scale_insight.current_state == "SMALL" then
          {
            focus: "FOUNDATION_BUILDING",
            target_growth_rate: "2-4 activities per week",
            priority: "Stability and core capabilities over raw growth",
            rationale: "Small scale requires solid foundation before scaling"
          }
        elif $scale[0].scale_insight.current_state == "MEDIUM" then
          {
            focus: "BALANCED_EXPANSION",
            target_growth_rate: "4-8 activities per week",
            priority: "Balance growth with stability, selective specialization",
            rationale: "Medium scale can support moderate growth while maintaining quality"
          }
        else
          {
            focus: "OPTIMIZATION_OVER_GROWTH",
            target_growth_rate: "Optimize existing, add strategically",
            priority: "Depth over breadth, improve success rates",
            rationale: "Large scale benefits more from optimization than expansion"
          }
        end
      ),
      
      # How we set the pace
      pace_setting_mechanisms: {
        reactive: {
          boredom_system: "Automatically works on improvements during idle time",
          failure_response: "Debug and fix failures as they occur",
          metrics_tracking: "Learn from every execution"
        },
        
        proactive: {
          regular_assessments: "Weekly/monthly health checks guide priorities",
          ratchet_cycles: "Systematic bottleneck identification and fixing",
          trend_analysis: "Validate continuous improvement trajectory"
        },
        
        strategic: {
          human_direction: "Strategic goals and priorities set by developers",
          capacity_planning: "This assessment informs growth decisions",
          selective_growth: "Choose which capabilities to develop based on goals"
        }
      },
      
      # Recommended pace for current conditions
      recommended_pace: (
        if $growth[0].tradeoff_analysis.recommendation | contains("SLOW_DOWN") then
          {
            action: "STABILIZATION_PHASE",
            target: "0-2 new activities per week, focus on improving existing",
            duration: "2-4 weeks",
            success_criteria: "Stability score >75%, success rate >70%"
          }
        elif $growth[0].tradeoff_analysis.recommendation | contains("ACCELERATE") then
          {
            action: "GROWTH_PHASE",
            target: "5-8 new activities per week, maintain stability >80%",
            duration: "4-8 weeks",
            success_criteria: "Add 20-30 quality activities while maintaining metrics"
          }
        else
          {
            action: "BALANCED_PHASE",
            target: "3-5 new activities per week, improve 2-3 existing per week",
            duration: "Ongoing",
            success_criteria: "Steady growth with stable success rates"
          }
        end
      )
    }
  }
' > $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/pacing-strategy.json
```

## Output

Create: $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/growth-strategy-complete.json

task_steps.description: Generate comprehensive report answering all philosophical and practical questions

prompt.template:
Generate comprehensive boredom and growth management report:

## Create Report: $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/BOREDOM_AND_GROWTH_ASSESSMENT.md

```markdown
# Boredom System & Growth Management Assessment

**Generated**: [timestamp]
**Purpose**: Answer fundamental questions about identity, scale, growth, and pacing

---

## Part 1: Boredom System Status

### Configuration
- **Idle Threshold**: [X] minutes
- **Check Interval**: [X] seconds
- **Status**: [ACTIVE | CONFIGURED_BUT_UNUSED | DISABLED]

### Activity Queue
**Total High-Gradient Activities**: [count]

**Priority Breakdown**:
```

tasks.description: Assess boredom system configuration, queued activities, and operational status

prompt.template:
Assess the boredom/idle improvement system:

## 1. Boredom Manager Configuration

```bash
# Check if boredom manager is active in codebase
cd repos/metabob-opencode
grep -A 20 "IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS\|CHECK_INTERVAL_MS" packages/opencode/src/session/boredom-manager.ts

# Configuration values
IDLE_THRESHOLD=$(grep "IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS" packages/opencode/src/session/boredom-manager.ts | grep -oP '\d+ \* \d+ \* \d+')
CHECK_INTERVAL=$(grep "CHECK_INTERVAL_MS" packages/opencode/src/session/boredom-manager.ts | grep -oP '\d+ \* \d+')

echo "Idle Threshold: $IDLE_THRESHOLD ms"
echo "Check Interval: $CHECK_INTERVAL ms"
```

## 2. Boredom Activity Queue

```bash
# Query backend for current boredom activities
if curl -s http://localhost:8080/health 2>&1 | grep -q "ok\|healthy"; then
  echo "Backend available - querying boredom activities..."
  
  # Try to fetch boredom activities via API
  curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/activities/boredom \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"limit": 20}' 2>&1 | jq -r '.' || echo '{"activities": [], "error": "API not available"}'
else
  echo "Backend not available - checking file-based approach"
fi > $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/boredom-queue-raw.json

# Analyze activities with high improvement gradient
cd ~/.metabob/activities
jq -s '
  map(select(.estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient > 0.3)) |
  sort_by(-.estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient) |
  map({
    template_id: .id,
    improvement_gradient: .estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient,
    success_rate: .estimated_metrics.success_rate,
    execution_count: .estimated_metrics.execution_count,
    avg_cost: .estimated_metrics.avg_cost,
    priority_category: (
      if .estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient > 0.7 then "CRITICAL"
      elif .estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient > 0.5 then "HIGH"
      elif .estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient > 0.3 then "MEDIUM"
      else "LOW" end
    )
  })
' *.json > $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/high-gradient-activities.json
```

## 3. Recent Boredom Activity Triggers

```bash
# Check for boredom activity execution logs
if [ -f ~/.local/share/opencode/boredom-activity-log.json ]; then
  jq '{
    total_triggers: length,
    last_7_days: map(select(.timestamp > (now - 604800))) | length,
    last_30_days: map(select(.timestamp > (now - 2592000))) | length,
    most_recent: (sort_by(-.timestamp) | .[0] | {activity_id, timestamp, success})
  }' ~/.local/share/opencode/boredom-activity-log.json
else
  echo '{"total_triggers": 0, "status": "No boredom activity log found"}'
fi > $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/boredom-trigger-history.json

# Check OpenCode logs for boredom activity mentions
if [ -f ~/.local/share/opencode/log/dev.log ]; then
  grep -i "boredom\|idle" ~/.local/share/opencode/log/dev.log | tail -20 > $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/boredom-log-excerpts.txt
fi
```

## 4. Improvement Candidates Analysis

```bash
# Templates that would benefit from boredom-triggered improvement
jq -s '
  map(select(.estimated_metrics.execution_count > 0)) | {
    total_templates: length,
    needs_improvement: map(select(.estimated_metrics.success_rate < 0.7)) | length,
    critical_improvement: map(select(.estimated_metrics.success_rate < 0.5 and .estimated_metrics.execution_count >= 3)) | length,
    never_executed: map(select(.estimated_metrics.execution_count == 0)) | length,
    high_cost: map(select(.estimated_metrics.avg_cost > 0.5)) | length,
    
    # Categorize by improvement potential
    by_potential: {
      critical: map(select(.estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient > 0.7)) | length,
      high: map(select(.estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient > 0.5 and .estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient <= 0.7)) | length,
      medium: map(select(.estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient > 0.3 and .estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient <= 0.5)) | length,
      low: map(select(.estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient <= 0.3 or .estimated_metrics.improvement_gradient == null)) | length
    }
  }
' ~/.metabob/activities/*.json > $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/improvement-candidates.json
```

## 5. Boredom System Health

```bash
# Overall system health assessment
jq -n --slurpfile queue $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/high-gradient-activities.json \
       --slurpfile history $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/boredom-trigger-history.json \
       --slurpfile candidates $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/improvement-candidates.json '
  {
    boredom_system_status: (
      if ($history[0].total_triggers > 0) then "ACTIVE"
      else "CONFIGURED_BUT_UNUSED" end
    ),
    idle_threshold_minutes: 5,
    check_interval_seconds: 30,
    
    activity_queue: {
      high_gradient_count: ($queue[0] | length),
      critical_priority: ($queue[0] | map(select(.priority_category == "CRITICAL")) | length),
      high_priority: ($queue[0] | map(select(.priority_category == "HIGH")) | length),
      top_candidate: ($queue[0][0] // null)
    },
    
    trigger_history: $history[0],
    
    improvement_pipeline: $candidates[0],
    
    system_health: {
      has_work_to_do: (($queue[0] | length) > 0),
      is_triggering: ($history[0].last_7_days > 0),
      backlog_size: ($queue[0] | length),
      utilization: (
        if ($history[0].last_30_days > 0) then
          ($history[0].last_30_days / 30.0)  # avg triggers per day
        else 0 end
      )
    }
  }
' > $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/boredom-system-assessment.json
```

## Output

Create comprehensive assessment: $ACTIVITY_TEMP_DIR/boredom-system-assessment.json

Must include:
- boredom_system_status: ACTIVE | CONFIGURED_BUT_UNUSED | DISABLED
- activity_queue: {count, priorities, top_candidate}
- trigger_history: {total, recent, last_trigger}
- improvement_pipeline: {needs_improvement, by_potential}
- system_health: {has_work, is_triggering, backlog_size, utilization}
